summary: E2E tested CSV import dialog (Admin › Menu › Importer CSV) with 6 scenarios covering comma & semicolon delimiters, BOM+accented headers, missing/invalid columns, invalid rows, and price parsing tolerance. parseCsv() rewrite works flawlessly (all preview parsing is correct: delimiter auto-detection, BOM strip, accent/case-insensitive header aliases, CHF suffix + comma-decimal price, empty-row filtering, missing-column error toast). HOWEVER, submit() has a CRITICAL blocker: POST /api/products returns 422 for EVERY row because the payload sends `image_url: null` when the CSV image cell is empty (line 743: `image_url: r.image_url || null`). The backend Pydantic Product model declares `image_url: str = ""` and rejects None. Verified via network capture: 2 successive 422s on happy-path submit. The user-facing errors panel shows `[object Object]` instead of readable messages because axios `err.response.data.detail` is an array of ValidationError dicts and is not stringified. My initial toast-substring check produced false PASS results because the phrase '2 produit'/'importé' also appears in the submit button label ('Importer 2 produits') and in the failure toast ('Aucun produit importé'); confirmed with GET /api/products/all + network POST status inspection that no products were actually created.

minor.issue: Requires admin auth (returned 401 from in-page fetch even after admin login) — the auth cookie may be HttpOnly with strict SameSite; not a bug per se but worth confirming intended access model for admin-only listing.

ui_bugs.issue: Sends image_url: null when CSV image column is empty. Backend Product model requires str — every POST fails with 422. Fix: change `image_url: r.image_url || null` to `image_url: r.image_url || ""` (Admin.jsx line ~743).

Renders `[object Object]` in errors panel when backend returns Pydantic 422 (detail is an array of dicts). Fix: stringify — e.g. `typeof detail === 'string' ? detail : JSON.stringify(detail)` or map to `d.msg`.

integration_issues.flow: CSV import happy path (all 3 delimiter/encoding variants)
integration_issues.issue: Preview parses correctly and shows expected rows, but submit fails 422 for every row → 0 products created; success toast '{n} produit(s) importé(s)' never fires (only failure toast 'Aucun produit importé — n erreur(s)').

issues: Console warning: DialogContent missing Description/aria-describedby (accessibility). Non-blocking but should add <DialogDescription> or aria-describedby.

action_items: CRITICAL FIX in /app/frontend/src/pages/Admin.jsx line ~743 (CsvImportDialog submit): change `image_url: r.image_url || null` to `image_url: r.image_url || ""`. This unblocks the entire CSV import feature.

Improve error stringification in same submit(): the `[object Object]` messages hide the real reason. Suggest: ```const detail = e?.response?.data?.detail; const msg = typeof detail === 'string' ? detail : Array.isArray(detail) ? detail.map(d => d.msg || JSON.stringify(d)).join('; ') : (detail ? JSON.stringify(detail) : e.message);```
Optionally, relax backend Product model in /app/backend/server.py line 90 to `image_url: Optional[str] = ""` for defensive parity — but the frontend fix is sufficient.
Add DialogDescription to CsvImportDialog (and other DialogContents) to fix a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: parseCsv() implementation (Admin.jsx ~L650-704) is solid: BOM strip, delimiter auto-detect (per-line semicolon vs comma count), quoted CSV field state machine, header key normalization (NFD accent strip + lowercase + non-alphanumeric strip), alias lookup, tolerant price parser, empty-row filter — matches the E1 spec and all 6 preview scenarios pass.
submit() has payload/type mismatch with backend Product model — sending null for image_url string field. This must have never worked end-to-end during dev testing.
Error panel renders raw axios error detail objects — always guard with JSON.stringify or map to .msg for Pydantic detail arrays.
Category matching (norm() with NFD strip + lowercase) is correct and matches 'Antipasti', 'Primi Piatti' as expected.
Admin.jsx is 1683 lines — should be split (OrdersTab, ReservationsTab, MenuTab, CsvImportDialog, BulkUploadDialog, etc. into separate files) for maintainability.

To detect real success vs false-positive, do NOT rely on substring matching in body text ('2 produit' appears in submit-button label 'Importer 2 produits' AND failure toast 'Aucun produit importé'). Instead: (a) inspect network responses for POST /api/products and check status===200, or (b) confirm the errors panel [data-testid='csv-errors'] is absent/empty AND toast has data-type='success', or (c) check the products list via UI. Also verify the fixed error stringification renders human-readable text (not '[object Object]'). Admin login is at /Angel/login, dashboard at /Angel/dashboard.
rca of the issue: REPRODUCTION: Login /Angel/login as AngelCED26/CE26$Lucc → Menu tab → 'Importer CSV' → upload comma CSV `name,price,category,image\nCSV_A_Test,7.50,Antipasti,` → click 'Importer 2 produits'. RESULT: Failure toast 'Aucun produit importé — 2 erreur(s)' and errors panel shows '• Ligne 2 (CSV_A_Test) : [object Object]'. Network shows POST /api/products → 422. RCA: In Admin.jsx submit() the payload is `{ ..., image_url: r.image_url || null, ... }`. When r.image_url is '' (empty image cell), `|| null` yields null. Backend Product Pydantic model at /app/backend/server.py:90 declares `image_url: str = ""` which does not accept None (Pydantic strict type). Response: 422 with detail=[{loc:['body','image_url'],msg:'Input should be a valid string', ...}]. Frontend catch block does `e?.response?.data?.detail || e.message` — detail is an array (truthy Object) → falls into template string → '[object Object]'. MITIGATION: (1) Change `image_url: r.image_url || null` → `image_url: r.image_url || ""` in Admin.jsx submit(). (2) Improve error stringifier: `const d = e?.response?.data?.detail; const msg = Array.isArray(d) ? d.map(x => x.msg || JSON.stringify(x)).join('; ') : (typeof d === 'string' ? d : (d ? JSON.stringify(d) : e.message));`. (3) Optionally make backend field Optional[str] for defense-in-depth.
